Consider the following PR description:
Interval merging logic broken for adjacent intervals

#### Description

The interval merging function `canMerge16` is incorrectly determining when two intervals can be merged. This affects operations that rely on interval consolidation in run containers.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/RoaringBitmap/roaring/v2/roaring64"
)

func main() {
    // Create a bitmap and add some values that should form adjacent intervals
    rb := roaring64.New()
    
    // Add values that create adjacent intervals: [0,5] and [6,10]
    for i := uint64(0); i <= 5; i++ {
        rb.Add(i)
    }
    for i := uint64(6); i <= 10; i++ {
        rb.Add(i)
    }
    
    // These should be merged into a single interval [0,10]
    // but the merging logic is broken
    fmt.Printf("Cardinality: %d\n", rb.GetCardinality())
    fmt.Printf("Contains all values 0-10: %t\n", rb.ContainsRange(0, 11))
    
    // The issue becomes apparent when doing operations that trigger merging
    rb2 := roaring64.New()
    rb2.Add(0)
    rb2.Add(11)
    
    result := roaring64.Or(rb, rb2)
    fmt.Printf("Union result cardinality: %d\n", result.GetCardinality())
}
```

The merging logic fails to properly identify when intervals are adjacent and can be combined, leading to incorrect bitmap operations and potentially corrupted internal state.
